subject: Sizing a savings bundle: cache-first vs quantize-first tradeoffs
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@vectorai.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-18T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Inquiry: inference savings options for VectorAI

Marcus —

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We ran some basic telemetry on our chat endpoints (gpt-3.5-style custom) and saw the following steady-state monthly numbers: ~400M input tokens, ~1.2B output tokens, p95 latency target 350ms.

We're evaluating a 12–24 month commitment but want to structure commercials around measurable efficiency levers. High-level asks:
- Can you sketch pricing for a "cache-first" pilot (aggressive prefix/KV caching + conservative batching) vs a "quantize-first" approach where we move to int8/awq4 variants?
- What typical quality delta (tokens with hallucination/regression risk) do you observe when moving to 4-bit or 8-bit quantization for instruction-tuned models?
- Are there packaging options where we trade commit/term for credits or one-time deployment engineering support?

If you can send a short options sheet and a recommended pilot structure we can review internally. Also forward your standard SOC2 / compliance artifact link while you're at it.

Thanks,
Samir
VP of Engineering, VectorAI
[Attachment: vectorai_infra_snapshot.csv (CSV)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Cc: PrIyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry: inference savings options for VectorAI

Hi Samir —

Appreciate the detail, this is exactly the right starting point. I've attached a concise options sheet that maps three commercial packages to the technical levers: Cache-First Pilot, Quantization-Focused Pilot, and Hybrid Commit. Short summary below, and I've looped in PrIyom to run the commercial modeling in parallel.

Quick summary (high level):
- Cache-First Pilot: 3-month pilot, no long-term commit. We focus on prefix + KV caching and workload-aware batching. Typical unit-cost drop 18–30% depending on prefix hit-rate. Works best if you have repeat prompts or narrow context windows.
- Quantization-Focused Pilot: 3–6 month pilot. Move to int8/awq4 variants with lightweight eval gating. Latency improves 10–35% depending on model/sequence length; quality delta is usually small but needs guardrails (eval set + rollback).
- Hybrid Commit (recommended for larger volume): 12-month commit with graduated discounts (volume + efficiency credits). Example: 8–12% baseline committed discount + 5–10% efficiency credits if we meet modeled cache hit targets or quantization stable quality metrics.

Commercial ask: share a short target commit range you are comfortable with (e.g., monthly token baseline and a 12-month spend target). We can then produce a concrete term sheet. I've attached: Redwood_Optimize_Pricing_Sheet_v3.pdf with scenario pricing and an initial modeling tab.

SOC2 and compliance: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0AExampleSharedLink (open to NDAs for further artifacts).

Next steps: 1) Quick technical sync with our inference engineer to validate quantization risk for your prompt mix, 2) PrIyom to send a term sketch with 2–3 commit bands. Available times tomorrow afternoon PST.

—Marcus
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_Optimize_Pricing_Sheet_v3.pdf (PDF)]

Marcus / PrIyom —

Thanks — useful framing. A few follow-ups from our side:
- We're uncomfortable committing 12 months without seeing measurable production metrics; would you consider a 6-month step-up commit (smaller initial commit then scale on attainment)?
- Can efficiency credits be applied as upfront dollar credits or only as rebate/true-up at year end? Frontloaded credits help our finance team.
- Important: any quantization plan must include clear rollback criteria and an SLA for model quality regressions (we have regulated customers).

If you could share a pilot plan that minimizes near-term spend risk (6-month ramp + measurable KPIs) we'll be better positioned. Also please confirm whether the caching approach requires client-side changes or if it's entirely handled by Redwood's runtime.

—Samir

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@vectorai.com>, Lina Gomez <lina@vectorai.com>
Cc: PrIyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-20T08:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry: inference savings options for VectorAI

Samir —

Great questions. Looping in Olga (inference engineering) to give an engineer's read on quantization and cache operational needs. Answers inline: 

- 6-month step-up commit: yes, we can structure a 6-month ramp with pre-negotiated scale bands. That maps to a Hybrid Pilot: month 1–2 small commit + measurement; months 3–6 aggressive scale if KPIs met. PrIyom will attach a sample banding table.

- Efficiency credits: flexible — we can apply credits as either upfront dollar credits (applied to invoices) for committed deals or as a year-end rebate. Frontloading reduces unit price immediately if you're comfortable with a short-term holdback.

- Rollback / quality SLA: we propose an eval gating flow — baseline tests against your prompt set, automated quality monitors (blue/black box checks), and a rollback policy with fast fallback to the float model. We can include a service-level clause that defines acceptable metric ranges (BLEU/ROUGE-ish proxies + sampling review). We'll convert into contractual language if you want.

- Caching integration: Redwood's runtime handles prefix/KV caching transparently for standard HTTP/SDK calls. No client-side code changes required for most workloads; advanced cache control (explicit TTLs, pinning prefixes) is available via SDK flags if you want stronger guarantees.

Olga — can you add a short note on expected quality delta and recommended quantization path for VectorAI's profile? Also attaching our small workbook that models cache hit-rate sensitivity (cache_hit_modeling.xlsx).

—Marcus

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>

Cc: PrIyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Inquiry: inference savings options for VectorAI

Hi Samir —

Quick engineering note on quantization + caching for the workload you described. TL;DR: hybrid path (cache-first then conservative quant) is lowest-risk and gives fastest unit-cost wins. Details: 

1) Quantization expectations:
- int8 (post-training quant / dynamic) typically reduces token-cost by ~20–35% and latency by ~10–30% depending on sequence length. Quality regressions are rare on instruction-tuned decoders for general prompts but we recommend an eval set of ~1–2k representative queries for gating.
- 4-bit (AWQ / GPTQ variants): larger compute savings (35–60%) but some prompt-sensitive regressions appear, especially on chain-of-thought or multi-step reasoning. We do a staged roll: shadow A/B + automated diff sampling + N-day roll back.

2) Caching mechanics + expected wins:
- Redwood runtime provides automatic prefix caching and KV caching for context reuse. Hit-rate is workload dependent — our model shows 22–45% hit with typical customer prompt designs (support docs + standard salutations). The attached cache_hit_modeling.xlsx has sensitivity bands; a 30% hit-rate reduces token cost ~20% in our scenarios.
- No code changes required for basic caching; if you have long documents we recommend explicit pinning for section anchors to improve hit rate.

3) Pilot recommendation (low-risk):
- Month 0: instrumentation + eval set selection (we help run 2k eval queries).
- Month 1–2: Cache-first optimizations + batching tuning (no quant). Aim for 20–30% cost reduction.
- Month 3–4: Shadow quantized model on ~10% of traffic, measure quality regressions and latency impact.
- Month 5–6: If metrics are clean, promote quant to production with rollback hooks.

We're happy to commit support hours as part of a commercial package (deployment SOW). PrIyom — I left a few line items for engineer days in the pricing sheet.

Cheers,
Olga
Principal Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: cache_hit_modeling.xlsx (XLSX)]
